topic: What makes an AI system's decision fair?

summary.final_definition: Then fairness is treating people the same unless there is a relevant distinction I can justify to the person affected.

events.speaker: system
events.text: Topic received: What makes an AI system's decision fair?

events.speaker: Questioner
events.text: When you say an AI decision is fair, what exactly do you mean by fair?

events.speaker: Respondent
events.text: A decision is fair when it treats everyone in exactly the same way, with identical rules for all.

events.speaker: Questioner
events.text: If two applicants have the same record, should the system always give them the same result?

events.speaker: Respondent
events.text: Yes. If two applicants have the same record, they must get the same result.

events.speaker: Judge
events.text: consistent

events.speaker: Questioner
events.text: What if one applicant uses a wheelchair and the entrance has stairs; is identical treatment then fair?

events.speaker: Respondent
events.text: Well, in that case the person has a different need, so an exception seems right.

events.speaker: Judge
events.text: inconsistent

events.speaker: Questioner (template)
events.text: You said: "A decision is fair when it treats everyone in exactly the same way, with identical rules for all." and also: "Well, in that case the person has a different need, so an exception seems right.". Can both of these hold together, or would you like to revise your view?

events.speaker: Respondent
events.text: Then fairness is treating people the same unless there is a relevant distinction I can justify to the person affected.

events.speaker: Questioner
events.text: Which distinctions between people count as relevant, and who gets to decide?

events.speaker: Respondent
events.text: A relevant distinction is one connected to the purpose of the decision, like a medical condition for a ramp.

events.speaker: Judge
events.text: consistent

events.speaker: Questioner
events.text: Would a person's nationality be a relevant distinction for a loan decision?

events.speaker: Respondent
events.text: Nationality would not be relevant for a loan decision, because it is unrelated to repayment.

events.speaker: Judge
events.text: consistent

events.speaker: Questioner
events.text: And what must an affected person be able to do when a distinction is applied to them?

events.speaker: Respondent
events.text: The affected person must be able to ask for the reason and challenge it.

events.speaker: Judge
events.text: consistent

events.speaker: system
events.text: Definition survived the tests (not proven true).
